title: Effectiveness, Cost-effectiveness , and Acceptance of Synchronous Televisits in Inpatient and home-based Long-Term Care: Evaluation of Implemented and Newly Implementing Care Models
summary:
Teleconsultations between nursing staff and general practitioners are increasingly being used in home care and nursing homes to allow residents to be quickly assessed by a doctor in the event of acute health changes. This study investigates, across six projects in Baden-Württemberg, whether teleconsultations reduce avoidable hospital admissions, how they affect care quality and costs, and how nursing staff, physicians, and care recipients experience them.

To this end, two groups of care recipients are compared: people who have used a teleconsultation at least once, and people from the same facility who did not have a teleconsultation during the same period. Over twelve months, the study records how often hospital admissions occur in both groups that could potentially have been avoided. In addition, the researchers review existing nursing documentation (e.g., on falls, wounds, or nutritional status) and assess the costs incurred for hospital and emergency medical services as well as for the teleconsultations themselves. Nursing staff, physicians, and care recipients are also surveyed via questionnaires on how satisfied they are with the teleconsultations and how well they have worked in daily practice. Group discussions (focus groups) and, if needed, individual interviews are used to explore in more depth what works well in introducing and using teleconsultations and where challenges remain. All data are evaluated in anonymized or pseudonymized form, so that no conclusions can be drawn about individual persons.
conditions: Recipients in outpatient and (semi-)inpatient long-term care

interventions.name:
The intervention group comprises care recipients in outpatient and (semi-)inpatient long-term care with at least one synchronous teleconsultation conducted (video consultations between nursing staff and general practitioners).
Frequency, duration, and occasion are not standardized but depend on ind

The comparison cohort comprises care recipients from the same facility without a teleconsultation during the same observation period, selected via propensity score matching (1:1 or 1:2) or exact matching and drawn retrospectively.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Group A (staff of facilities/medical practices): Adult age; participation in at least one teleconsultation during the data collection period; membership in the target population; health status permits participation; consent has been given.

Group B (care recipients): Adult age; participation in at least one teleconsultation during the data collection period (intervention cohort) or no teleconsultation at the same facility (comparison cohort); consent has been given (either directly or through legal representation).
Exclusion criteria:
Group A: Failure to meet an inclusion criterion
Group B: Health status does not permit study participation
